title: Separable-root divided differences give polynomial annihilators
statement:
Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $\iota:L\to R$ be a unital ring homomorphism. For $G=\sum_jc_jT^j\in L[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $t\in R$ write $G(t)=\sum_j\iota(c_j)t^j$. Suppose $\alpha\in L$ and $P\in L[T]$ satisfy $P(\alpha)=0$ and $P$ is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. For each $G=\sum_jc_jT^j\in L[T]$ define the polynomial
$$D_{G,\alpha}(T)=\sum_{j\geq1}c_j\sum_{h=0}^{j-1}T^{j-1-h}\alpha^h,$$
where both sums are finite because the coefficients of $G$ have finite support. The following identities hold in $L[T]$ and $L$:
$$G(T)-G(\alpha)=(T-\alpha)D_{G,\alpha}(T),\qquad D_{G,\alpha}(\alpha)=G'(\alpha).$$
Put $Q=D_{P,\alpha}$. Then
$$P=(T-\alpha)Q,\qquad Q(\alpha)=P'(\alpha)\ne0.$$
For every $t\in R$ with $P(t)=0$ and every $F\in L[T]$ with $F(\alpha)=0$, put $H=D_{F,\alpha}$. One has
$$F=(T-\alpha)H,\qquad Q(t)F(t)=P(t)H(t)=0.$$
These assertions allow $F=0$, all characteristics, and the zero ring $R$.

source.place: Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, finite primitive-element calculation and general algebraic-union paragraph

proof.text: All sums may be taken over a finite range containing the coefficient support. For each $j\geq1$, expand the product to get the telescoping identity $(T-\alpha)\sum_{h=0}^{j-1}T^{j-1-h}\alpha^h=\sum_{h=0}^{j-1}(T^{j-h}\alpha^h-T^{j-1-h}\alpha^{h+1})=T^j-\alpha^j$: consecutive terms cancel, leaving precisely the two endpoints. Multiplying by $c_j$ and summing gives $(T-\alpha)D_{G,\alpha}=G(T)-G(\alpha)$; the $j=0$ term on the right is zero. These are identities of coefficient sequences with the polynomial multiplication of [def-weil-polynomial-ring], not merely identities of polynomial functions.

source.place: Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, finite-extension paragraph: the factorization P=(x-alpha)Q and Q(alpha) nonzero, with the elementary calculation made explicit

proof.text: At $T=\alpha$, each of the $j$ summands $T^{j-1-h}\alpha^h$ becomes $\alpha^{j-1}$, since $(j-1-h)+h=j-1$. Hence $D_{G,\alpha}(\alpha)=\sum_{j\geq1}j c_j\alpha^{j-1}=G'(\alpha)$ by the formal derivative formula of [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Here $j c_j$ means repeated addition, so this calculation holds in every characteristic, also when $\alpha=0$ (powers of exponent zero equal $1$).

source.place: Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, finite-extension paragraph: the factorization P=(x-alpha)Q and Q(alpha) nonzero, with the elementary calculation made explicit

proof.text: With $G=P$ the first two steps and $P(\alpha)=0$ give $P=(T-\alpha)Q$ and $Q(\alpha)=P'(\alpha)$. By [def-pc-separable-polynomial], separability supplies $U,V\in L[T]$ with $UP+VP'=1$. Evaluating this equality at $\alpha$ gives $V(\alpha)P'(\alpha)=1$. Evaluation preserves products directly from the convolution formula: for $A=\sum_i a_iT^i$ and $B=\sum_j b_jT^j$, $(AB)(\alpha)=\sum_{i,j}a_ib_j\alpha^{i+j}=(\sum_i a_i\alpha^i)(\sum_j b_j\alpha^j)$, and it preserves sums and $1$ coefficientwise. If $P'(\alpha)=0$, the displayed equality would give $0=1$, contradicting [def-weil-field]. Thus $Q(\alpha)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, finite-extension paragraph: the factorization P=(x-alpha)Q and Q(alpha) nonzero, with the elementary calculation made explicit

proof.text: For $F(\alpha)=0$, Step 1 with $G=F$ gives $F=(T-\alpha)H$. More generally the evaluation in $R$ satisfies $(AB)(t)=\sum_{i,j}\iota(a_i b_j)t^{i+j}=(\sum_i\iota(a_i)t^i)(\sum_j\iota(b_j)t^j)=A(t)B(t)$, using that $\iota$ preserves products and $R$ is commutative. Consequently $Q(t)F(t)=Q(t)(t-\iota(\alpha))H(t)=((t-\iota(\alpha))Q(t))H(t)=P(t)H(t)=0$. If $F=0$, its defining coefficient sum gives $H=0$. No cancellation, division or nontriviality in $R$ was used, so the zero ring is allowed.
